claims.text: Send a CISO to the newsroom as a CISO, a data protection officer as a DPO, and one particular person as a persona made for them, with nothing but a link.
claims.quote: This is the brief for doing that with nothing but a link.

claims.text: Personas move out of the site's code into an encrypted vault opened in the reader's browser with a published read key, so the newsroom's agents can add or update one without a change to the site.
claims.quote: Personas move out of the site's code into an encrypted vault

claims.text: There are three kinds of link: a page of its own for the few personas everyone uses, a fragment for any number more, and a private persona in its own vault.
claims.quote: A page of its own for the few personas everyone uses

claims.text: The site is static pages on GitHub Pages, so no server can answer an arbitrary persona path; the fragment after the hash solves it.
claims.quote: The site is static pages on GitHub Pages, so there is no server to answer

claims.text: RFC 3986 says the fragment is separated before dereference and dereferenced solely by the user agent, so the browser keeps it and GitHub Pages never sees it.
claims.quote: the browser keeps it, and GitHub Pages never sees it

claims.text: A private persona lives in a vault of its own and the link carries the vault id and read key: whoever has the link can open it, whoever does not cannot find out it exists.
claims.quote: Whoever has the link can open the persona; whoever does not, cannot, and cannot find out it exists.

claims.text: When the link opens, the page shows who you are reading as, the newsroom opens as that persona, and the persona is added to the reader's personas straight away as a visitor.
claims.quote: The persona is added to the reader's personas straight away, as a visitor

claims.text: Follow keeps the persona linked to the vault and Make it mine forks it; the two halves come straight from git, tracking the upstream or branching from it.
claims.quote: Follow and fork are the two halves of the design, and they come straight from git

claims.text: The site already opens thirty-odd vaults in the browser with nothing but an endpoint, a vault id and a read key, so a persona vault is one more.
claims.quote: This site already opens thirty-odd vaults that way

value.unit: vaults the site already opens in the browser

claims.text: The newsroom's agents keep the personas: every published article is added to the personas it belongs to, every newsletter is a review, and each change is a vault commit with a line in changes.jsonl.
claims.quote: Keeping personas is one more job on the desk.

claims.text: Adding or changing a persona is an sgit commit and push to the vault, without a release of the website, a build or a deploy.
claims.quote: without a release of the website, a build, or a deploy

claims.text: A persona can later carry outside reading with sources, which is how a newsroom with sixty articles can serve a dozen audiences well.
claims.quote: That is how a newsroom with sixty articles can serve a dozen audiences well

claims.text: Netflix launched Profiles on 1 August 2013, up to five per account, so each person in a household got their own suggestions.
claims.quote: Netflix launched Profiles on 1 August 2013, up to five per account

claims.text: Bluesky's starter packs, launched 26 June 2024, each hold up to 150 people and three custom feeds and have their own link.
claims.quote: Each holds up to 150 people and three custom feeds, has its own link

claims.text: Starter packs are the closest thing to a link to a persona shipped at scale: the link is the onboarding, and what it sets up belongs to the newcomer afterwards.
claims.quote: the link is the onboarding, and what the link sets up belongs to the newcomer afterwards

claims.text: Mastodon's community follow packs were CSV files of up to 35 accounts, and the project has announced a native version whose people can opt out.
claims.quote: were CSV files of up to 35 accounts that a user downloaded and imported

claims.text: A persona about a person goes in a private vault and is sent only to them; a public persona describes a role, never a named individual unless they have agreed.
claims.quote: a public persona describes a role, never a named individual, unless they have agreed

claims.text: Apple News and Brave News personalise on the device but still run servers; here the content is static files and the personas ciphertext, and the difference is who holds the copy that travels.
claims.quote: the difference is who holds the copy that travels between devices

claims.text: A persona here is not a fictional user a team designs for; it is a reading list the reader wears and can change.
claims.quote: it is a reading list the reader wears, and can change

claims.text: Anyone with a private persona link can open it, the same as a forwarded email; the persona holds reading suggestions, not secrets.
claims.quote: the persona holds reading suggestions, not secrets

claims.text: The page says where a persona came from and marks any vault that is not the newsroom's own, so a forged persona cannot pass itself off as ours.
claims.quote: so a forged persona cannot pass itself off as ours

claims.text: There is no analytics, by design; what the newsroom will know is what readers send through the share page and whether people write back.
claims.quote: There is no analytics, by design.

claims.text: To build: the vault with a published read key, the pages, follow and fork and remove in the next SG Meter, a keeper role with a behaviour policy, private personas, and outside reading.
claims.quote: A newsroom role with a behaviour policy: what it may change, how it records each change

claims.text: It should be built at newsroom.sgit.ai after the reader account has moved; the vault and the schema can be made first.
claims.quote: The vault and the schema can be made first, because they do not depend on which site reads them.

claims.text: It demonstrates what the site is about: content that changes without a deploy, shared with those who hold the key, decrypted in the browser, kept by agents whose every change is a commit.
claims.quote: Content that changes without a deploy, shared with exactly the people who hold the key

claims.text: The article was written from a voice note by Dinis Cruz by a Claude Code session working as the newsroom on 10 October 2026.
claims.quote: by a Claude Code session working as the sgit.ai newsroom, on 10 October 2026

claims.text: Apple's and Brave's descriptions of their own products are their claims, not independent audits.
claims.quote: are their claims, not independent audits

claims.text: A link to the front page lands a reader on a page made for nobody: sixty-odd pieces across six topics, with no way to know which they would want.
claims.quote: they land on a page made for nobody in particular
